During pregnancy, treatment to normalize maternal blood 
glucose levels reduces the risk of adverse maternal, fetal, and 
neonatal outcomes. Extra glucose from the mother crosses the 
fetal placenta and the fetus’ pancreas responds by releasing ex-
tra insulin to cope with the excess glucose. The excess glucose is 
converted to fat, which results in macrosomia. The fetus may 
become too large for a normal birth resulting in the need for 
cesarean delivery. Neonatal hypoglycemia at birth is another 
common problem. The above normal levels of maternal glucose
